page: Amazon Web Services c9g.medium is an entry-tier compute-optimized virtual machine powered by AWS ARMv9 architecture featuring the Neoverse-V3 core. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 1 dedicated physical core delivering 1 vCPU at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. Memory is provisioned at 2.0 GB, resulting in a compute-oriented 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The CPU topology incorporates 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration supporting the AES instruction set.

The hardware configuration provides no bundled local instance storage and relies on network-attached storage solutions, supported by a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. Without hardware accelerators, the system operates with zero dedicated GPUs. In benchmark evaluations, the dedicated Neoverse-V3 core demonstrates distinct workload bifurcations. Single-threaded data compression tasks show strong results, highlighted by gzip compression achieving 36.12 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching 16.83 GB/sec. Conversely, overall synthetic benchmarks reflect the limitation of a single execution thread, yielding modest multithreaded and general computational throughput across tests such as PassMark and multi-core stress-ng.

Memory bandwidth measurements demonstrate 38.46 GB/sec large-block read and 13.36 GB/sec large-block write speeds. Application-level evaluations show Redis handling 3.3 million SET operations per second and static web throughput measuring 4.13 GB/sec. Small language model inference on a 135M parameter model registers 84.44 tokens per second during text generation. From an operational efficiency perspective, the dedicated ARM core provides consistent per-cycle execution without multi-tenant thread contention, making it an efficient option for lightweight processing tasks.

The c9g.medium is best suited for single-threaded processing tasks, continuous integration workers, microservices, lightweight web servers, and edge data compression routines where predictable single-core performance is required within a low-footprint compute envelope.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.medium is an entry-level compute-optimized instance based on the ARMv9 architecture and AWS Neoverse-V3 processors running on the Nitro hypervisor. It offers 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU operating at 3.3 GHz, paired with 2.0 GB of memory and 48 MB of L3 cache. The instance excludes local storage and discrete GPUs, operating with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. In benchmark tests, the instance shows remarkable single-threaded compression performance, achieving 36.12 GB/sec in gzip compression and 16.83 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, while overall multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth reflect its single-thread limitations. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures reliable execution without hyperthreading interference. Due to its balanced compute ratio and modest resource profile, c9g.medium is suited for lightweight microservices, isolated build pipelines, single-threaded batch processing, and low-traffic network services.
